discovery: Production and quantum control of ultracold molecules, including direct laser cooling and trapping of molecules

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: For decades molecules resisted the methods that brought atoms to ultracold temperatures. Their rich internal structure blocks closed optical cycling. The nominees overcame this and made molecules fully controllable quantum systems. DeMille showed direct laser cooling of a diatomic molecule (SrF, 2010) and then magneto-optical trapping of molecules. Doyle invented buffer-gas beams, which made such experiments possible, and extended laser cooling to CaF and polyatomic molecules, including trapping molecules in optical tweezers. Ye, with the late Deborah Jin, created the first quantum-degenerate gas of ground-state polar molecules (KRb) and revealed dipolar interactions and ultracold chemistry. Together these advances opened a new field. Ultracold molecules now serve as quantum simulators, qubits, probes of chemistry at the quantum limit, and precision tests of fundamental symmetries, notably the ACME electron-EDM bounds. These bounds constrain physics beyond the Standard Model at energies beyond colliders.
